title: Initial commit
description: Vue 2.6.11, Storybook 5, webpack. At this point it is a canvas playground and a Mapbox experiment more than a design system.

title: First dark theme
description: Dark theme variables and a real set of button classes — the first hint of a system rather than a sandbox.

title: Storybook 6
description: Upgrade lands and every story is rewritten against the new format.

title: Tailwind experiment
description: Tried, and quietly dropped. The token approach won instead.

title: Vue 2 → Vue 3
description: "i guess i'm sticking with vue 3." Twenty components make the jump.

title: Charts arrive
description: Highcharts wired in, with a stacked-bar and sequence palette to match.

title: "tokens!"
description: The design-token era begins — the idea the whole styles package is eventually built on.

title: Atomic design, day one
description: Components reorganised into atoms, molecules and organisms.

title: Atomic design, day six
description: "it's a no to atomic design LOL" — and then, in the very next commit, "removed all traces of atomic design."

title: Notifications
description: A store-backed notification system with a notification center, built over about a week of steady iteration.

title: Split into packages
description: "major movements done, working." The repo becomes a multi-package workspace. Forty components at this point.

title: epicenter-styles
description: Tokens and SCSS split into their own package — one source of truth, compiled to CSS.

title: Docs separated
description: Documentation moves out of the component package and into its own tree.

title: v1.0.3
description: Forty-six components, forty-six stories. Every component finally has one.

title: Storybook 8 + Vite
description: Off webpack. The dev loop gets dramatically faster, which sets up the month that follows.

title: Color rebuilt on chroma.js
description: The palette stops being hand-picked hex values and starts being generated.

title: VitePress docs
description: A real documentation site, alongside Storybook rather than inside it.

title: The script setup sweep
description: Components converted to Composition API one at a time across May — 207 commits, the busiest month in the project's history.

title: React starts
description: A second Storybook on port 6007 and three .tsx files. More intent than implementation.

title: Icon pipeline
description: icons.json drives an SVG download, clean and generate step that emits framework components.

title: Docs generate themselves
description: vue-docgen-api reads props, slots and events straight from source. An accessibility addon lands two days later.

title: React goes quiet
description: The React Storybook's build step is removed. Still three .tsx files — and it stays that way for fourteen months.

title: useTheme
description: Theme switching becomes a composable instead of scattered logic.

title: Icons v1 deleted
description: The old icon component and its build script are removed; per-icon components replace the icon map entirely.

title: 2.0.0-beta opens
description: The version line that the current library still sits on.

title: light-dark()
description: Theming rebuilt on the CSS light-dark() function — both themes defined in one declaration instead of two.

title: React restarts
description: The package is re-initialised from scratch and the old React icon component dropped. Second attempt, in earnest this time.

title: TypeScript
description: The component packages convert to TypeScript.

title: Two frameworks, officially
description: Renamed to epicenter-components-<framework>, icons split into -vue and -react. React goes from 3 files to 110 inside a week.

title: "initial move complete"
description: The React port reaches feature coverage with Vue.

title: Storybook 10
description: Both instances upgraded together — the first upgrade that had to account for two frameworks.

title: Landing page and shared helpers
description: A landing site, plus storybook-shared for the helpers both Storybooks now need.

title: React gets its own intro
description: The React Storybook stops being the second-class instance and gets a front door of its own.

title: Conventions written down
description: AGENTS.md and then CLAUDE.md capture the rules that had been living in one person's head — including the Vue/React parity requirement.

title: v2.0.0-beta.1 published
description: The packages ship to GitHub Packages. Both frameworks release together.

title: The custom property contract
description: Tokens, a naming grammar and a validator that fails the build. The styles package stops relying on discipline and starts enforcing.

title: Dropdown on native popover
description: Rebuilt on the popover API and CSS anchor positioning — then patched around three Safari paint bugs.

title: Parity, in practice
description: EpEnrichmentDropdown repaired and EpContextualLookup ported to match Vue. 126 React files, and the two frameworks moving together.
